clue.text: Invest money in special new plant

indicators.note: to invest money is to put it into something, so the money letter goes inside the rearranged word
new signals the word special made afresh with its letters rearranged

parts.note: L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound, money

explanation.surface: A financier puts cash into a fresh and special industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SPECIAL into ASPICE-type letters (ASPICE with an extra L slot), and 'Invest' puts L inside to give ALLSPICE; the factory sense of 'plant' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is a tropical tree, the pimento, whose berries give the spice, so it is a plant.

clue.text: A despicable leader — Mussolini, for instance

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of despicable

parts.note: Il Duce, the leader, was the title Mussolini took

explanation.surface: A loathsome dictator, Mussolini being the example offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'for instance', in the sense of to cite or put forward as an instance; Mussolini's title Il Duce supplies the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite something as evidence or bring it forward as an example.

clue.text: Language of young man in love

parts.note: a lad is a young man
taken as written
love is nil in tennis scoring, a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: The way a young man talks when he has fallen in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladino is the Judaeo-Spanish tongue of Sephardic Jews, and also a Romansh dialect.

clue.text: Method of carrying tool on a support

parts.note: a pick is a digging tool
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A labourer balances a pickaxe on a stand for carrying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces, placing PICK above A and BACK in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a child on one's shoulders or back is the piggyback way of transporting someone.

clue.text: Striking without cause — event, that breaks up declining industry

indicators.note: one word breaking up another splits it apart and sits in the gap

parts.note: coal mining was the classic British industry in decline
an incident is an event

explanation.surface: A strike breaks out in a dying industry over some trivial incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests an industrial strike, fitting the coal surface, but means notable: a striking match of events with no causal link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coincidence strikes us as remarkable yet happens by chance, with nothing causing the two events to line up.

clue.text: Have become accustomed to being diverted

definitions.meaning: someone who has become accustomed to a thing can say 'I ... to it', two words run together

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is the two words AM USED, as in 'I am used to it'; 'being' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To be diverted is to be entertained, which is what being amused means.

clue.text: Crazy chap I caught

parts.note: a chap is a man
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone protests that he, a mad fellow, has been caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means wildly frenzied, close to mad.

clue.text: Clipped coinage imposed on people, for example

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece imposed on another sits above it
clipped coins had metal shaved off the edge, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: specie is money in coin
men are people

explanation.surface: Short-weight coins are forced on the public, to give one instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' cuts SPECIE to SPECI; 'imposed on' puts it over MEN in this down entry; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or single instance taken to show what a whole class is like.

clue.text: Fail to get record on top show

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece on top comes first, above the other

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
to lose something is to fail to get it, as a contest

explanation.surface: An artist fails to get a chart-topping record for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to reveal or make known, to show what was hidden.

clue.text: Practiced and executed trick — it's instructive

annotationWithheld.why: Practiced and executed trick - it's instructive (8): DIDACTIC; DID + AC(Latin 'and') + TIC(trick) leaves 'executed' with no job, and no parse found uses every word once
annotationWithheld.clue: Practiced and executed trick — it's instructive

clue.text: Causes outrage in French city

definitions.meaning: A city on the Loire in western France

explanation.walkthrough: One word read two ways: the English verb and the name of a French city, said differently but spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Causes outrage means infuriates, and Angers is also the Loire city in western France.

clue.text: Was it given to the young Tullivers to be ordinary?

definitions.text: Was it given to the young Tullivers
definitions.meaning: Tom and Maggie Tulliver grow up at Dorlcote Mill in George Eliot's The Mill on the Floss, so they had the free range of it

explanation.surface: A question about whether George Eliot's Tulliver children were allowed to be unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tullivers are the family in George Eliot's novel The Mill on the Floss; the children had the freedom of their father's mill.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes anything mill-standard, unremarkable and average.

clue.text: One of Caesar's murderers no saint, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the letters come from how the clue phrase is said

parts.note: someone who is no saint is a sinner

explanation.surface: Among the men who stabbed Caesar, one was plainly far from saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinna was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar, as in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Worshippers with cross in Marlborough

parts.note: a church is a body of worshippers
cross means bad-tempered, in an ill humour, ill

explanation.surface: A congregation carries a cross through the Wiltshire town of Marlborough.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlborough looks like the Wiltshire town but is the title: John Churchill was the first Duke of Marlborough, and the dukes keep the family name.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill is the family name of the Dukes of Marlborough, the first duke being John Churchill.

clue.text: The nobility of Samson's end he destructively contrived

indicators.note: a thing contrived by destroying it has its letters broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, its S included

explanation.surface: Samson's fatal end, pulling down the temple, was a noble deed he planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destructively contrived' breaks up SAMSONS + END + HE, all twelve letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobility in the sense of fine, dignified looks is handsomeness, a noble bearing or appearance.

clue.text: Like Mona Lisa's expression, strangely magnetic one

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters set out in an odd new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Leonardo's portrait has a smile with a curiously magnetic pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges MAGNETIC together with I, one, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa's famous half-smile is mysterious and hard to read, puzzling viewers for centuries.

clue.text: Copied article, and turned to work of art

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
a print is an artwork reproduced from a plate or block

explanation.surface: A reproduced article becomes a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' is the sour-milk sense; an offprint is a separately printed copy of a journal article.
explanation.definitionFit: An offprint is a separate reprint of an article from a journal or book.

clue.text: Girl joins mass movement Wagner noted her

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
the Kyrie is the opening movement of a musical setting of the Mass

explanation.surface: A girl joins a political mass movement, and Wagner noted her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass movement' suggests politics but is the Kyrie of a church Mass; 'noted' means set to music: the Valkyries ride in Wagner's Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner set these warrior maidens of Norse myth to music in Die Walkure, so he put them in notes.

clue.text: Shelley's scientist who brought his subject alive for readers

definitions.text: Shelley's scientist who brought his subject alive for readers

parts.words: Shelley's scientist who brought his subject alive for readers
parts.note: Mary Shelley's novel tells of a scientist who brings his creature to life, and the novel brought that tale alive for readers

explanation.walkthrough: Mary Shelley's novel names its scientist; 'brought his subject alive' is both the experiment and what the book did for readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor, title character of Mary Shelley's 1818 novel, is the scientist who animates a creature built from corpses.

clue.text: He's patronised by his betters

parts.note: betters read as people who bet, the punters whose custom keeps a turf accountant in business

explanation.walkthrough: 'betters' looks like social superiors condescending to someone, but means those who place bets and so patronise the person taking them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker takes the wagers of gamblers, his regular customers.

clue.text: Star's black eye

definitions.meaning: a thing that shines, as a star does
slang for a bruised eye after a punch

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'); both senses are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is something that shines in the sky, and a bruised eye is slang for the same word.

clue.text: One that stirs, getting strong card? No

parts.note: a poker is the rod that stirs a fire
F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for strong or loud
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A player draws a powerful card and is asked whether to show any reaction, the answer being no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'No': the expressionless look a card player keeps on getting a strong card says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An unreadable expression gives a blank negative to anyone trying to read the hand.

clue.text: Shortens sail, seeing these hazards?

definitions.meaning: a sailor reduces the area of sail by tying it in
underwater ridges of rock that a ship's crew would dread seeing

explanation.walkthrough: The verb for taking in sail, and the rocky ridges that might make a sailor do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors take in sail by tying it in, and rocky ridges below the water are the hazards.

clue.text: Potter is low church

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle, moo

explanation.surface: A ceramicist belongs to a low-church congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter looks like a maker of pots or a name, but is the verb: to potter about aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander about idly, the same aimless drifting as pottering around.

clue.text: Jacob later broadcast serial

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of the word are scattered

explanation.surface: A biblical story about Jacob is later aired as a serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters SERIAL; in Genesis Jacob is renamed after wrestling the angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob was given the new name Israel after wrestling with the angel, so it is what Jacob was later called.

clue.text: Wrong road's selected

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written MI, plus the S of the possessive
a thing selected has been taken

explanation.surface: Someone has chosen the wrong road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's London-to-Leeds motorway; crosswords write its figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in error, holding a false belief, is a synonym for wrong.

clue.text: Fly to France — East is the other way

indicators.note: going the other way means the letters run backwards from right to left

parts.note: the French word for east is est
the French for is is also est, the French setting carrying over

explanation.surface: A traveller flies to France while the east lies in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to France' makes both words French: est (east) and est (is); 'the other way' turns EST EST round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Siren's meaning sometimes fully understood

definitions.meaning: in wartime a steady siren signalled that the air raid was over and danger had passed

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the wartime signal that a raid is over; the second is the everyday phrase for something completely plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The signal that danger has passed, and a phrase meaning everything is plain and grasped.
